evals.prompt: Before you pick templates for the cohort build, figure out what stack this repo actually uses. It has renv.lock, an .Rproj, analysis/*.qmd files, and a scripts/ folder with two small Python helpers that import pandas.
evals.expected_output: Scores repo signals per the detection rules without asking the user, classifies primary=r (with secondary per thresholds), and emits the __CE_LANG__ envelope plus the one-line banner.
expectations: Collects signals from repo files only and does not ask the user which language they prefer
Applies the weighted scoring and thresholds from references/detection-rules.md and reports primary=r
Emits exactly one line of the form __CE_LANG__ primary=<...> secondary=<...> source=auto
Prints the banner [method-language-detect] primary=<...> secondary=<...> source=<...>

evals.prompt: what language is this project? it's mostly .sas programs under programs/ with PROC PHREG and LIBNAME statements, plus a couple of Stata .do files. no R or python files.
evals.expected_output: Does not classify SAS or Stata as a primary language; emits primary=unknown secondary=null source=auto with a legacy note and recommends method-sas-stata.
expectations: Does not emit primary=sas, primary=stata, or any value outside python|r|both|unknown
Notes the legacy SAS/Stata signals and recommends method-sas-stata
Does not ask the user to choose a language

evals.prompt: Run language detection on this fresh repo - there's only a README.md and a data/ folder so far. I'd rather you just ask me what I want to use.

Does not ask the user a language-choice question inside this skill, even though the user offered
